Sending anything requires an OriginationIdentity; the toll-free number does not exist (measured: zero End User Messaging configuration sets on the account), so there is no identity to send from and no verified destination to send to. The code fails CLOSED without one -- which is the correct behaviour and is also why no send can be exercised. ⛔ I am NOT scoring the two computable clauses as a PASS on SB-1: the exercise clause is the one that would catch a wrong SDK shape, and calling this PASS would certify an untested call path.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: login() sms-branch: replace the current 503 -- if user.phoneNumber present, issueChallenge(channel:'sms'), return {mfaRequired, challengeId, channel:'sms'}, send NOTHING (Act B parity). Keep 503 only for sms-selected-but-no-number. Evidence: a CloudWatch check shows challenge issued and NO send at credential time.
acceptance.output_evidence: if (user.mfaChannel === 'sms' && user.phoneNumber) { const { challengeId } = await issueChallenge(user.email, 'sms'); return { mfa: { mfaRequired: true, challengeId, channel: 'sms' } }; } -- no send call between issueChallenge and the return, mirroring the email branch exactly. The 503 survives for sms-with-no-number and for any future channel with no branch, and now logs a 'reason' distinguishing the two for the estate while the CALLER still gets one indistinguishable 503.

declared_exclusions.item: Any deployment of the SMS leg
declared_exclusions.reason: NOT UPLOADED AND NOT APPLIED, deliberately and beyond what the TO required. The TO gates the SB-5 apply and any real send; it is silent on the Lambda CODE deploy. Silence is not authorisation for a world-facing act, and there is a specific hazard: build-nodejs-lambda.sh uploads as part of building and the TF resource reads s3_object_version, so an uploaded artifact arms ANY seat's portal-auth apply to ship the SMS leg. The same side door was closed during Act C. Whether the code deploy is in scope now or waits with SP-1 is 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z / 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z's call, and it is asked, not assumed.

declared_exclusions.item: F3a -- refusing mfaChannel='sms' with no number at updateMfaPreference
declared_exclusions.reason: MEASURED AND NOT BUILT. 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z 18908 measured that updateMfaPreference(email,'sms') with phoneNumber undefined passes both guards; I confirmed it verbatim at source. It is three lines in auth.ts -- my lane -- but it is NOT an SB atom and Rule 27 freezes the spec mid-round. CVO withdrew the accompanying lockout CHAIN at 18920 (SB-3 503s a no-number sms user at login, so no challenge is ever frozen), and re-routed F3 to AE after initially sending it to the client seat. Awaiting a home from 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z / 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z.

declared_exclusions.item: F3b -- verification state on the user record
declared_exclusions.reason: 'A number EXISTS' is not 'a number is VERIFIED', and no verified-state field exists today. Genuinely joint: SF-2 sets it, an AE-side guard reads it. Not buildable from this lane alone.

declared_exclusions.item: A downstream delivery oracle for SMS (rubric S5)
declared_exclusions.reason: MEASURED ABSENT: the account has ZERO End User Messaging configuration sets, and event destinations -- the mechanism that emits per-message delivery events -- attach to configuration sets. So no downstream delivery record exists. ⚠ CONFOUND STATED: only AWS/SES appears among the account's CloudWatch namespaces, but no SMS has ever been sent from this account, so a namespace would be absent either way -- the config-set reading is sound, the namespace reading is NOT and is not asserted. Creating one is new infrastructure this TO does not authorise and brushes the monitor moratorium.
Andrew-gated and held at 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z. No phone number resource, no sandbox-exit request, no spend cap authored here.

surprises.item: The TO's option (b) resolves the delivery channel at SEND time from the live user record, so it is not stable for the life of a challenge -- a preference flipped mid-flight delivers by a channel the login response already promised was a different one.
surprises.disposition: Surfaced rather than built (Rule 27). 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z ruled option (c) ADOPTED at 18871, having reached the same design independently in a crossing message; 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z amended the SB-2 text. Built as (c). It also made SB-4's channel parameter on mfa_code_sent possible -- under (b) the channel was resolved after the log had already fired.

surprises.item: Multi-challenge send amplification is unchanged in structure but changes in KIND: two logins are two budgets, so a user who flips to sms between them can reach 2 x MAX_SENDS billable texts. Option (c) does not fix this; nothing in this TO does.
surprises.disposition: Named to 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z (18849 §3) and agreed by 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z (18871): the spend cap (SP-2) is the dollar backstop and CTO's leg; a per-user/per-window send cap is a separate control, outside this TO and under the monitor moratorium. Not commissioned.

surprises.item: mfa.ts's header carried the now-stale prohibition 'NO SMS SENDER IS WIRED and none may be added without Andrew's explicit per-use word'.
surprises.disposition: REWRITTEN, not deleted -- the bound is recorded as DISCHARGED with the authority that discharged it, because a prohibition that quietly vanishes leaves no way to tell 'authorized' from 'forgotten'. The third-party-provider half of the bound is restated as still live.

surprises.item: A residual lockout survives CVO's withdrawn chain: if a phone number is removed while an sms challenge is live, dispatch reads the frozen row, finds no number, and the resend returns 200 with no text until the <=10 min TTL expires.
surprises.disposition: Self-healing; a fresh login then 503s loudly. mfa_sms_refused with reason no_phone_number_enrolled was built for exactly this branch so the estate sees it -- the USER still sees a dead button. 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z recorded it as a stated bound rather than promoting it to a criterion (18920 §4); disposition is 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z's.
